implementation_summary: F-051: runAuditCrawl now calls pinSiteHosts() before any request (robots.txt included) and before any browser. It resolves the start host once with safe-net resolvePublic and fails closed with a new exported AuditCrawlRefusedError (code ERR_PRIVATE_ADDRESS or ERR_UNREACHABLE, the reachability.ts wording, no addresses). It also resolves the www twin (isSameSite treats it as the same site): pinned to its checked address when public, MAP <twin> ~NOTFOUND otherwise. An IP-literal start needs no rule. A hostname that is not a plain DNS name (WHATWG URL accepts ',' and '*') is refused before lookup, so resolver rules cannot be injected. The crawl launches its own Chromium through a new deps.launchBrowser seam (default chromium.launch, headless) with BrowserManager's flags plus --host-resolver-rules for exactly those hosts (IPv6 bracketed). It never reads browserPolicy.pinned. The browser is closed in finally (success, error, abort) with a 3 s cap. F-052: the context is created with serviceWorkers 'block', viewport 1440x900, baseURL, ignoreHTTPSErrors true. A shared machine's global browserPolicy.guard is still installed when set (parity with createContext). The deps.browserManager fixture seam is kept for existing tests. Coordinator addition: AuditCrawlResult.robots?: Pick<RobotsPolicy,'isAllowed'> carries the policy the crawl fetched, for BE-305's link check (F-054).

risks: Behaviour change: an existing test changed form. 'by default the public-only guard stops every request to a loopback address' expected pages [] and now expects AuditCrawlRefusedError ERR_PRIVATE_ADDRESS with zero contexts and site.requests []. Guard coverage moved to a new DNS-rebinding test with the original assertions.

API addition: runAuditCrawl can now throw AuditCrawlRefusedError (exported via the barrel to @qa/core). The runner route (not mine) maps any crawl throw to AUDIT_CRAWL_FAILED and could surface err.code/err.message instead.
deps.browserManager is a fixture-only seam: no pins, no service-worker block. Production (runner) passes no deps; confirm no caller sets it.
CHROMIUM_ARGS and the two refusal messages are copies of browser.ts / reachability.ts (not exported there): drift risk.
Hosts other than the start host and its www twin (CDNs, off-site redirect targets) are still resolved by Chromium itself after the guard's lookup: the residual risk ADR 0014 accepts.
A browser that hangs on close is left after 3 s (same as BrowserManager.close).
Performance: one Chromium launch per audit plus 1-2 DNS lookups before the crawl.
handoff: runAuditCrawl now owns its Chromium (deps.launchBrowser seam, default chromium.launch) pinned to the start host and www twin via --host-resolver-rules, with serviceWorkers 'block'. It never uses BrowserManager or browserPolicy.pinned. It throws AuditCrawlRefusedError { code: 'ERR_PRIVATE_ADDRESS' | 'ERR_UNREACHABLE' } before any request when the start host no longer resolves public. The runner could show that code instead of the generic crawl-failed message. AuditCrawlResult.robots (Pick<RobotsPolicy,'isAllowed'>, optional) is ready for BE-308/BE-192 to pass to BE-305's link check (F-054). No migrations, no dependency changes; browser.ts and safe-net.ts unchanged.
